checks: No eclipse at 6 of 48 covered epochs where the 2.67128 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 392559026 is an eclipsing binary candidate with an orbital period of 2.6713 days. Automated analysis of TESS photometry detected a primary eclipse causing 4.30% dimming and a secondary eclipse at 5.7 sigma significance near orbital phase 0.49, yielding a strong BLS detection signal-to-noise of 90.1. Pixel-level difference imaging confirmed the signal with a peak signal-to-noise of 30.6, though the centroid offset of 2.7 arcsec from the target warrants attention. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be a previously uncatalogued system. The pipeline's machine learning screening assigned a score of 0.41 (on a 0 to 1 scale), and the candidate passed all data quality checks without flags.
